entities.summary:
Cisco Systems, Inc. is an American multinational technology conglomerate founded in 1984 by Leonard Bosack and Sandy Lerner at Stanford University. The world's leading manufacturer of networking hardware and software, Cisco's routers and switches built the physical infrastructure of the internet, earning it the title 'the plumber of the internet.'

Bosack and Lerner created the first multi-protocol router allowing different computer networks to communicate, directly solving the challenge of connecting Stanford's disparate computing networks. This technology scaled into the commercial internet's backbone as Cisco's products became the standard for routing internet traffic globally. During the dot-com boom, Cisco briefly became the world's most valuable company at $555 billion in March 2000.

Cisco's acquisitions of hundreds of smaller networking and security companies allowed it to expand from routers and switches into cybersecurity, collaboration tools (WebEx), and data center virtualization. The company's networking certifications (CCNA, CCIE) became globally recognized credentials for network engineers. Cisco's market capitalization collapsed 86% during the dot-com bust as router orders dried up, but the company survived and regained importance as internet infrastructure continued expanding. Its hardware underpins corporate networks, cloud providers, and government communications globally.
